reviews.title: Stubborn developers refuse to offer emergency access feature
reviews.text: Nearly every other mainstream password manager offers an emergency access feature where you can set up trusted contacts where they can trigger a request which can be rejected by you by email to prevent access or after a set amount of time, they will be given access to your passwords. This is a excellent way to ensure your digital legacy and ensure your loved ones can gain access to your passwords if you are incapacitated or no longer around.  In communication with the developers for many years, they still refuse to implement this. They want you to write down your special key and your password on a single sheet of paper and give it to someone, which not only gives them the ability to get into your account right now, but if that were to get lost or in the wrong hands is a major security issue. This alone has caused me to leave the 1Password software and not go back until they fix this, which at this point in time I don’t have any faith they will ever fix because they don’t seem to care about it making it more secure.  Disappointing because otherwise it’s a good app and service.

While it does safely store and sync passwords (that gets 2 stars) 
Examples that prevent additional stars Include :
- constantly admin you to save a new password when it’s just logged you in with the password it had stored (so no change initiated)
- constantly asking you to save a passkey but then it doesn’t update it in the right place and then it’s impossible to merge it with an existing item that should have the passkey (passkeys really aren’t prime time in 1p)
- generating a new password but not showing you all the existing locations where you could save it (no longer has a search box to let you override where it thinks it should go)
- duplicate list of password items to use

It’s rather sad and alternatives like Apple passwords are increasingly looking more reliable.

reviews.title: Please fix search
reviews.text:
A very annoying bug has returned to the iOS app. It was fixed for a few months but recently reared its ugly head again. Here are the steps to reproduce because obviously the 1Password QA team can’t be bothered to do any kind of real world testing.

1.) Open 1Password on iOS and navigate to a list of entries  (eg All Items or Archive)
2.) Click into the search field
3.) Type search criteria

Expected result:
1.) Every character typed into Search is visible in the search field
2.) Search results are returned with each keystroke 

Actual result:
1.) The first 3 or 4 characters are deleted after being typed and only the following characters are entered into search. 
2.) Search results are returned only for the characters entered. 

My guess on why this is happening: 
I began typing into the search field very quickly after launching the app. There seems to be a lag of around 5 seconds after launch where 1Password queries the server for changes (e.g. updated passwords, new passwords, etc.). If I search while those results are being returned from the server, then 1Password will null out the search criteria while it pulls in the changes. After the changes are pulled in, then subsequent search criteria I enter is properly logged. 

Sorry if this isn’t a clear enough description of what’s happening, but that’s the best I can do. You should be able to figure it out. 

This is just poorly designed UI/UX and a frustrating experience for power users who open and quickly search for what the

I attempted to contact 1Password for support multiple times over 2 days and ran into hurdles with their AI bot before I would get to a form to submit a ticket. Still 48 hrs and NO reply. Finally on the 3rd day I got an email essentially blaming me, saying I must have been a sucker to a phishing email or something - which I was not. I got a text message from Nigeria! that this login was hacked & by that time the email address was changed and a passkey put on it. I had no means to regain access to the account. Did 1Password offer to investigate? Or try to help me get access to this account back? NO 😡 What support was I paying for then?!? Adding this lack of any help to the recently announced price increase - I’M DONE.  You have LOST a long time customer. I will be moving to another password management platform. My subscription is CANCELLED.

Terrible UI, there is simply nothing good to say about this app. Deleted before trial ended, couldn’t face opening it again.

reviews.title: Zero customer support
reviews.text:
I’ve contacted customer support 3 times over the course of over a week now. Still no reply despite me highlighting that it’s an urgent issue.

I’d strongly advise against signing up with 1password as it’s impossible to get any support.

reviews.title: Been using for years
reviews.text:
Great password manager that I personally enjoyed using over the last few years.

As of today though, I have cancelled my subscription after a price hike that makes it more expensive than its competitors. A price hike that was reasoned down to “added value,” a technique they use to convince you it’s for a good reason.

Considering apples latest password manager update has made it a worthy contender, I have migrated to using that. 

1Password have become greedy.

They have shot themselves in the foot as a small increase I would have swallowed BUT  this increase as made me and I am sure many others look at better alternatives. By By

reviews.title: Not happy
reviews.text:
I’ve been a loyal 1Password user since around version 2 or 3, sticking with it through many upgrades over the years. For a long time, I accepted that its interface felt clunky and less intuitive than it could be, assuming the complexity was a necessary trade-off for top-tier security. That changed when I saw colleagues seamlessly using competitors like NordPass, Bitwarden, or Dashlane. Their apps felt modern, straightforward, and genuinely user-friendly, with smooth upgrades and minimal friction. Meanwhile, my experience with 1Password remains frustrating.
The real breaking point came with the upgrades themselves. Transitioning from 1Password 4 to 5 then 6 to 7 was a multi-step painful ordeal, despite the help docs being well written, actually following them proved confusing and time consuming. Now, with 1Password 8 requiring a full migration involving extra steps for older standalone vaults, I’ve reached my limit and decided to switch to a different password manager.
For these reasons; outdated user experience, cumbersome upgrades, and unnecessary complexity, I don’t recommend 1Password.
